cheek 0.3.1 removes redundant work before downloads start.

- Reuse complete HTML responses instead of requesting the same page again. Partial HTML responses still fetch the full page when needed.
- Probe up to three media candidates concurrently while preserving their original priority.
- Reuse the configured HTTP connection pool from resolution through downloads and playlist entries, including drained small probe responses.
- Reuse a Glyph playlist entry's title and artist instead of loading the playlist HTML again for each song.
- JSON timing events separate resolution, per-entry resolution, download, cover loading and postprocessing. Cover loading overlaps downloading; a slow cover timeout is reported separately.
- Add regression tests for HTML request counts, playlist metadata reuse and a byte-exact 4 MiB download using one pooled connection from resolution to completion.
- Extend the benchmark with a controlled 4 MiB resolution fixture. Local fixture results do not establish YouTube Music latency improvements on Android.

The existing supported sources and yt-dlp fallback remain. r-dlp is not integrated in this release. Includes Linux, Windows, macOS and all three Android binaries. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
